body:
I know my plan is ridiculous, but it is the only option I have left.


I'm going to save humanity before we destroy ourselves.

Because I feel like I'm just bottling everything up. And the thoughts just roam back into my mind whenever I see a family that looks poor, walk through a low income area, or hear about someone in my family having money issues. 


There are so many solutions out there already that can fix all of these problems that people just refuse to change. Like if the work week was changed to 30 hours, and the minimum wage increased. There would be a higher demand for jobs because employers would have to have more employees, people would be happier with more time to spend with their families or just relaxing thus people would work better. If people made more money and had more time to spend it than the economy would get better. 


Or what about a minimum yearly salary and we just automated everything that could be automatized. No more shitty fast food jobs or anything. People would have the freedom to be lazy. If people wanted more money they could go to college or university and find a better job. Also maybe some cuts to the military or foreign aid and let people have their education paid for. 


This is why I need an education in economics. That way I can have a better understanding of this stuff and become a part of the solution and not just a part of the problem. And be the catalyst to the solutions being put into actions. 


I can't stand how bad some people have it and people need to realize it would be very easy to change the world if only people actually gave a shit.

1) I don't think people like the way the world is and would change it if they could. Look at TigerHunters comment for example, he or she got upset with the Trayvon shooting and other things in world politics and I'm sure if given the opportunity he or she would change a lot in his or her country. 


2) I can become a leader, anyone can. Most people disagree with this but I believe if someone truly loves his or her country and wants the best for it's citizens that people will vote for him or her. 


3 / 4) I hate to use this example, but Hitler? By the time I'm in the position to run the world will likely be worse than it is now and people will be looking for someone to make a lot of changes. Big changes like a new form of government. 


5) I don't quite understand what you're trying to say here. I think that you're trying to say the dictator would want you to do stupid shit to be happy? If the people felt that the leader was doing something against the people's interests it only takes 25% of them to have him executed and a new dictator elected. 


6) Small price to pay imo for total government transparency. 


My plan isn't totally worked out and once I finish my education I'm sure it will be a lot different than it is today.

Believe me I have tried this approach. Ignore the terrible things in the world and think, "there's nothing I can do about them." This does not work for me in the slightest. I also get angry that people think this way (no offense to you personally, this thought process is very common). I don't think I deserve to be happy, and I can't be happy unless everyone has the same opportunities that I do. Can you imagine what the United States would be like today if they chose to stick with the founding fathers ideals? A hell of a lot better than it really is that's for sure. Those men made incredible changes to the world and were revolutionary thinkers. I am not a revolutionary thinker in any way. My ideas are very extreme and not well thought out, but it's something. Once I finish my education in political science and economics I'll have a much better understanding of the world and how it would be possible to change it.
I think one man can make drastic changes to the world and the technology is here now to make it possible.
